promises.text: 2024 campaign: Said he would "Lower real estate taxes and eliminate wasteful spending."
2024 campaign: Said he would "Implement an environmental infrastructure reconstruction program focused on rebuilding our wastewater" systems.
2024 campaign: Said he would "Streamline the county's Engineering, Public Works and Building departments to increase efficiency" and "speed permitting and cut departmental red tape."
2024 campaign: Said he would "Implement a program of real estate tax credits to encourage affordable, market-based housing development."
2024 campaign: "I will lead the charge to rebuild our environmental infrastructure."
2024 campaign: "We should eliminate sales taxes on the cost of materials for housing, to help make housing more affordable."
2024 campaign: On transit: "we should decrease and limit the use of large buses," shifting toward technology-based, point-to-point service.
2024 campaign: On home rule: "Our cities must be allowed to develop or redevelop as determined by their residents, not by politicians in Tallahassee."
2024 campaign: After the election, wrote on Facebook that "Pinellas County needs rebuilding now and I can't wait to roll up my sleeve and get the job done."
2024 campaign: Did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 Candidate Connection survey.

electionHistory.text: 2024 general, County Commission District 1: won. Chris Scherer (R) 262,740 (52.98%); Joanne 'Cookie' Kennedy (D) 233,197 (47.02%).
2024 Republican primary, District 1: canceled; Scherer advanced without appearing on the ballot.
Assumed office Nov 19, 2024; current term ends Nov 21, 2028.

keyPositions.text: Voted no on the $312.5 million Rays stadium bond resolution, which passed 5 to 2 on Dec 17, 2024.
Before the Dec 17, 2024 bond vote, pushed for another delay, saying the commission should not vote on bonds until the Rays met all conditions.
On the Rays deal after his election (Nov 2024): "We are in a new era right here," adding that "whatever was agreed to before needs to be looked at differently now."

votes.headline: Refused to hold a hearing on a dredge permit appeal in Palm Harbor
votes.inShort: Declined a request for a public hearing to appeal a county dredge and fill permit for 106 Harbor Drive. The county attorney said hearing the appeal was up to the board.
votes.officialTitle: Request for a public hearing to appeal the issuance of County Dredge and Fill Permit No. WND-24-00077 for 106 Harbor Drive, Palm Harbor.
votes.motion: A motion was made by Vice-Chair Scott, seconded by Commissioner Flowers, that the item be denied. The motion carried by the following vote:

does.text: Turned down the neighboring owners' (the Myrbacks') request for a public hearing to appeal a county dredge and fill permit issued July 19, 2024, for 106 Harbor Drive in Palm Harbor, which allows dredging of state-owned submerged land around a private dock and boat lift. With no hearing, the permit stands as issued; staff said it was properly issued after the dredge area was reduced to avoid seagrass.
